opportunities.name: arXiv topic search → Semantic Scholar citation count → save note
opportunities.description: For a given research topic and year, find the newest matching paper on arXiv advanced search, look it up on Semantic Scholar to get its first author and citation count, then add a summary line to the Notes app.
steps: Open arxiv.org and click Search, then Advanced search
Type {topic} in the Search term field (Title)
Tick the {subject} checkbox (e.g. Computer Science or Quantitative Biology)
Select the 'Specific year' radio and type {year}
Click Search and open the first result (newest announced)
Copy the paper title
Open semanticscholar.org, reject cookies if prompted, type the title into the search box and click Search
Open the matching result and read the first author and citation count
Open Notes, click 'New note', type '{topic} ({year}): {title} by {first_author}, {citations} citations' and press Enter

instances.values: topic='retrieval augmented generation', subject=Computer Science, year=2023 → RIGHT: Retrieval-augmented Generation for Mainstream Hashtag Recommendation, Run-Ze Fan, 11 citations
topic='protein structure diffusion', subject=Quantitative Biology, year=2024 → Accelerating Inference in Molecular Diffusion Models..., Ian Dunn, 7 citations
topic='graph neural networks traffic forecasting', subject=Computer Science, year not entered (abandoned before searching)

opportunities.name: Court case lookup on CourtListener + related statute on Cornell LII → save note
opportunities.description: For a given court case and related statute, find the case's citation and decision date on CourtListener, find the statute's section title on Cornell LII, and add a combined line to the Notes app.
steps: Open courtlistener.com (click the logo to go to the home page)
Type {case_name} in 'Keyword(s) search with operators' and press Enter
Open the matching Supreme Court result and read the U.S. Reports citation and decision date
Open law.cornell.edu, type {statute} in the search box and press Enter or click the search icon
Open the first U.S. Code result and read the section title
Open Notes, click 'New note', type '{case_name}: {citation}, decided {date}. See {statute} ({section_title})' and press Enter

instances.values: case='Carpenter v. United States' (585 U.S. 296, June 22, 2018); statute='18 U.S.C. 2703' (Required disclosure of customer communications or records)
case='Bostock v. Clayton County' (590 U.S. 644, June 15, 2020); statute='42 U.S.C. 2000e-2' (Unlawful employment practices)
case='Miranda v. Arizona' (1966); only the CourtListener part was done, no statute lookup or note

opportunities.name: Peerspace venue search by activity and city
opportunities.description: Search Peerspace for venues matching a given activity in a given city by choosing both from the autocomplete lists and running the search.
steps: Open peerspace.com (or click the search summary on the results page)
Click 'What are you planning?', select all, type {activity}
Pick the matching activity from the dropdown (unrecognised activities give an error)
Click 'Where?', select all, type {city}
Pick the matching city from the Google autocomplete list
Click Search and review the results

instances.values: activity='Team offsite' (not recognised), city='Chicago' (not recognised until the suggestion appeared)
activity='Birthday Party', city='San Francisco, CA, USA' → 467 results
